VeriSim is built on the AI Town codebase and is split into the following layers:

- **The server-side game logic in `convex/aiTown`**: This layer defines what state AI Town maintains, how it evolves over time, and how it reacts to user input. Both humans and agents submit inputs that the game engine processes `(ARCHITECTURE.md > Architecture > Overview)`.
- **The client-side game UI in `src/`**: VeriSim uses `pixi-react` to render the game state to the browser for human consumption `(ARCHITECTURE.md > Architecture > Overview)`.
- **The game engine in `convex/engine`**: Separated out from the AI Town-specific game rules to make it easy to hack on game rules. The game engine is responsible for saving and loading game state from the database, coordinating feeding inputs into the engine, and actually running the game engine in Convex functions `(ARCHITECTURE.md > Architecture > Overview)`.
- **The agent in `convex/agent`**: Agents run as part of the game loop and can kick off asynchronous Convex functions to do longer processing, such as talking to LLMs. These functions can save state in separate tables or submit inputs to the game engine to modify game state. Internally, agents use a combination of simple rule-based systems and talking to an LLM `(ARCHITECTURE.md > Architecture > Overview)`.

In the chest pain scenario, a clinical action from the test menu (such as an ECG) executes only if the patient's current trust state permits it (README.md > VeriSim 🏥 > Scenario: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" > The consent-gate mechanic). 

If the player orders an ECG before trust is earned:
- It produces an in-character refusal and a trust penalty (README.md > VeriSim 🏥 > Scenario: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" > The consent-gate mechanic).
- Pushing without repair makes Ray self-discharge, which is the scenario fail state (docs/persona_cards.md > VeriSim Persona Cards — Scenario 01: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" > Consent-gate rule (core mechanic)). Specifically, two refusals while hostile ends the scenario (README.md > VeriSim 🏥 > Scenario: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" > The consent-gate mechanic).

In the "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" scenario, the nurse character **Sam Okafor** behaves in the following ways:

* **Professional and Direct:** Sam is professional, direct, and quietly protective of patients with no time for vagueness (README.md > VeriSim 🏥 > Scenario: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3").
* **Execution of Instructions:** Executes clear, specific instructions promptly (e.g., `"bloods and a 12-lead"` leads to `"done"`), but pushes back on vague or unsafe orders (e.g., asking `"what am I sending the bloods for exactly?"`) (docs/persona_cards.md > VeriSim Persona Cards — Scenario 01: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" > NURSE — Sam Okafor).
* **Clinical Monitoring:** Flags deterioration (such as `"his sats are dropping, doctor"`) and will prompt the player if the patient is deteriorating and nothing is happening (docs/persona_cards.md > VeriSim Persona Cards — Scenario 01: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" > NURSE — Sam Okafor).
* **Escalation Triggers:** Escalates when ordered without rationale, or when the player ignores a flagged observation twice (docs/persona_cards.md > VeriSim Persona Cards — Scenario 01: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" > NURSE — Sam Okafor).
* **Support Levers:** Using clear SBAR-style communication earns proactive help, such as suggesting analgesia timing and chasing results faster (docs/persona_cards.md > VeriSim Persona Cards — Scenario 01: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" > NURSE — Sam Okafor).
* **Knowledge Boundary:** Holds full nursing competence, will not diagnose, but will hint through observations (docs/persona_cards.md > VeriSim Persona Cards — Scenario 01: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" > NURSE — Sam Okafor).
* **Voice:** Economical, using phrases like `"On it."` or `"Doctor — a word?"` (docs/persona_cards.md > VeriSim Persona Cards — Scenario 01: "Chest Pain, A&E Bay 3" > NURSE — Sam Okafor).

To run VeriSim's LLM on a Kaggle GPU, the goal is to run Ollama on a free cloud GPU and expose it over a tunnel so that VeriSim (running locally on your laptop) can use the GPU for inference (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > Running VeriSim's LLM on Kaggle GPU (or Colab)).

### Step 1: Set up the Kaggle Notebook
1. Go to `kaggle.com` and create a **New Notebook** (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > Running VeriSim's LLM on Kaggle GPU (or Colab) > Kaggle (recommended — 16 GB T4/P100, ~30h/week)).
2. In the right-hand **Settings** panel:
   * Set **Accelerator** to **GPU T4 x2** (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > Running VeriSim's LLM on Kaggle GPU (or Colab) > Kaggle (recommended — 16 GB T4/P100, ~30h/week)).
   * Set **Internet** to **On** (requires a phone-verified Kaggle account) (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > Running VeriSim's LLM on Kaggle GPU (or Colab) > Kaggle (recommended — 16 GB T4/P100, ~30h/week)).

---

### Step 2: Run the Notebook Cells in Order
Paste each block below into a separate cell and run them sequentially (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > Running VeriSim's LLM on Kaggle GPU (or Colab) > Kaggle (recommended — 16 GB T4/P100, ~30h/week)):

#### Cell 1 — Install `zstd`, install, and start Ollama
*(Note: Kaggle's notebook base image is missing `zstd`, which the Ollama install script needs for extraction)* (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > Running VeriSim's LLM on Kaggle GPU (or Colab) > Kaggle (recommended — 16 GB T4/P100, ~30h/week)).
```python
!apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq zstd
!curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
import os, subprocess, time
os.environ['OLLAMA_HOST'] = '0.0.0.0:11434'   # accept connections from the tunnel
subprocess.Popen(['ollama', 'serve'])
time.sleep(5)
print('ollama up')
```
(docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > Running VeriSim's LLM on Kaggle GPU (or Colab) > Kaggle (recommended — 16 GB T4/P100, ~30h/week) > Cell 1 — install zstd, install & start Ollama)

#### Cell 2 — Pull a model
*(A T4 16GB GPU handles models like `llama3.1:8b-instruct-q4_K_M` or `qwen2.5:14b-instruct-q4_K_M` at `q4`)* (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > Running VeriSim's LLM on Kaggle GPU (or Colab) > Kaggle (recommended — 16 GB T4/P100, ~30h/week) > Cell 2 — pull a model (T4 16GB handles these at q4)).
```python
!OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama pull llama3.1:8b-instruct-q4_K_M
```
(docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > Running VeriSim's LLM on Kaggle GPU (or Colab) > Kaggle (recommended — 16 GB T4/P100, ~30h/week) > Cell 2 — pull a model (T4 16GB handles these at q4))

#### Cell 3 — Open a public tunnel to the GPU
```python
!wget -q https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-linux-amd64 -O cloudflared
!chmod +x cloudflared
import subprocess, re, time, threading
proc = subprocess.Popen(['./cloudflared','tunnel','--url','http://localhost:11434'], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
def watch():
    for line in proc.stdout:
        print(line, end='')
threading.Thread(target=watch, daemon=True).start()
time.sleep(8)
print('\n>>> Look above for a https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL — send me that.')
```

#### Cell 4 — Keep the notebook awake
Leave this cell running to prevent the notebook from idling out (docs/kaggle_gpu_setup.md > !OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama pull qwen2.5:14b-instruct-q4_K_M > Cell 4 — keep the notebook awake (leave running)):

### Step 3: Point VeriSim at the Tunnel URL
Once Cell 3 outputs your `https://xxxxx.trycloudflare.com` URL, configure VeriSim's environment variables using the generated tunnel URL:


VeriSim's game engine loads and saves world state on each simulation step through the following flow:

1. The Convex scheduler calls the `convex/aiTown/main.ts:runStep` action (ARCHITECTURE.md > Architecture > Game engine (`convex/engine`) > Engine state management).
2. The `runStep` action calls `convex/aiTown/game.ts:loadWorld` to load the current game state, which invokes `Game.load` to retrieve all of a world's game state from the appropriate tables and returns a `GameState` object containing serialized versions of the players, agents, etc (ARCHITECTURE.md > Architecture > Game engine (`convex/engine`) > Engine state management).
3. The `runStep` action passes the `GameState` to the `Game` constructor, which parses the serialized versions of all the game objects into in-memory classes using their constructors (e.g., `new Player(serializedPlayer)`) (ARCHITECTURE.md > Architecture > Game engine (`convex/engine`) > Engine state management).
4. The engine runs the simulation forward, modifying the in-memory game objects (ARCHITECTURE.md > Architecture > Game engine (`convex/engine`) > Engine state management).
5. At the end of a step, the framework calls `Game.saveStep`, which computes a diff of the game state since the beginning of the step and passes the diff to the `convex/aiTown/game.ts:saveWorld` mutation (ARCHITECTURE.md > Architecture > Game engine (`convex/engine`) > Engine state management).
6. The `saveWorld` mutation applies the diff to the database, updates archived deleted objects if needed, updates the `participatedTogether` graph, and kicks off any scheduled jobs (ARCHITECTURE.md > Architecture > Game engine (`convex/engine`) > Engine state management).

The Ares stack is composed of the following agents:

*   **orchestrator agent** (with a hidden orchestrator persona that routes requests) (README.md > Ares > Architecture), (README.md > Ares), (.serena/memories/project/ares_overview.md > Ares project overview)
*   **coder agent** (README.md > Ares > Architecture)
*   **thinker agent** (README.md > Ares > Architecture)
*   **runner agent** (README.md > Ares > Architecture)
*   **Serena/code-navigation agent** (README.md > Ares > Architecture)

### How They Talk to Each Other

*   **Wiring & REPL Coordination:** `AresSystem` (`ares/system.py`) wires the agents together, along with memory, tracing, and learning. It also records which agent answered for ratings (.serena/memories/project/ares_overview.md > Ares project overview).
*   **A2A HTTP Services:** The agents expose A2A HTTP services running on ports `8100` to `8104` (`ares/a2a_server.py`), using `build_single_agent` (.serena/memories/project/ares_overview.md > Ares project overview), (README.md > Ares > Run).

With the `memory` extra installed, Ares recalls related memories before each prompt and adds them to the context. After each reply it hands the exchange to a small local model (`qwen2.5-coder:3b` by default) in the background, which pulls out facts worth keeping: your projects, tools, hardware, preferences and deadlines (devdesk_ares: README.md > Ares > Memory).

Everything stays in `~/.ares/memory`, and mem0's telemetry is switched off (devdesk_ares: README.md > Ares > Memory).

The Ares REPL supports the following slash commands:

- `/coder <task>`: code-focused task execution (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/thinker <task>`: deeper reasoning or planning (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/runner <task>`: quick execution-oriented task (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/serena <task>`: codebase-aware navigation and edits (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/good`, `/bad`: rate the last reply; Ares learns routing from it (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/learn`: show what Ares has learned about routing (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/remember <fact>`: store a fact verbatim (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/memories`: list what Ares remembers (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/forget`: delete all memories (asks first) (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/clear`: forget this conversation (long-term memory is kept) (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/help`: list commands (README.md > Ares > Commands)
- `/quit`: exit the REPL (README.md > Ares > Commands)

Ares learns routing through the `/good` and `/bad` rating commands (handled by `ares/learning.py`), which operate as follows:

- **Feedback Collection**: Rating a reply with `/good` or `/bad` saves the prompt and the agent that answered to `~/.ares/feedback.jsonl` as well as to the trace database at `~/.ares/traces.db` (README.md > Ares > Learning).
- **Orchestrator Integration**: The orchestrator's system prompt incorporates up to 8 well-rated and 8 badly rated routing examples so that similar requests are directed to the agent that previously succeeded (README.md > Ares > Learning). 
- **Scope of Learning**: Only routing is learned; tool sets and turn limits remain as configured because a few ratings cannot capture why an entire run succeeded or failed (README.md > Ares > Learning).
- **A2A Servers**: The A2A orchestrator picks up any new ratings whenever it restarts (README.md > Ares > Learning).

To run the five A2A agent servers in Docker, you can use the following commands:

```bash
docker compose -f docker/agents/docker-compose.yml up -d --build ARES_PROJECT=~/code/myapp
docker compose -f docker/agents/docker-compose.yml up -d # point /serena at a project
```
(README.md > Ares > Docker)

It is Linux only because it uses host networking, required because Ollama and Langfuse only listen on `127.0.0.1`. (README.md > Ares > Docker)
If Langfuse isn't running, Ares traces still go to `~/.ares/traces.db` (ares: README.md > Ares > Run).
